source.title: What Should Data Teach? Moving Bottlenecks Across Circuit, Store, and Use
source.authors: Yi-Xiao Chen; Ke Cheng; Jiang-Tao Guan; Shuo Huang; Yue Liu; Jun Zhang; Yue Liu; Jie Jiang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures formation of a binding–matching–transport read path and its dependence on data selection and ordering, using its own functional probes and training interventions. It does not reproduce the original induction-head or in-context-learning measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper tests an induction-style functional read path, including binding, matching, transport, and an induction metric. It does not directly test composition with a previous-token head, token-index loss as an in-context-learning measure, or a bump in the training loss. The paper's use of “induction-sensitive” and induction-style read-path terminology is not itself treated as a result. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: A data-curriculum paper that uses its own binding (previous-token), matching and transport probes. Three results bear on the claim. Pythia 160M runs show the functional induction-style path across runs and domains (V4). Data selection and ordering change when matching forms, with matching selectivity at 0.8B of 0.56 under Curriculum versus 0.014 under Ordinary (V5). Binding becomes usable before matching in both arms (V7). It does not study attention-only models, the loss bump, token-index ICL, or few-shot task heads.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. For this claim, add the authors' Circuit-stage results. A formation-time, Joint-to-matching prefix accelerates the binding–matching–transport path, and binding forms first. The early validation advantage persists to 100B tokens. The path is a role-level relation, not a fixed head set.
record.recipe_differences: Uses custom binding–matching–transport probes, mechanistic data selection, and training-order interventions; it does not reproduce the original induction-head circuit analysis or its in-context-learning/loss-curve measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on matching-teacher checkpoint, selection order, training arm, checkpoint, domain, and run. The paper reports the formation-time teacher outperforming endpoint-time selection on the relevant AUCs in some comparisons, but induction AUC reverses for Matching-only versus Joint-to-matching under the endpoint teacher.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-ranked head identities change during formation: no 0.3B head remains in the endpoint top-eight set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-like functional roles persist while the heads implementing them change over training.

record.problems: The functional probes are the paper's own operationalization and do not directly test canonical previous-token-head composition. The induction-related tables report no uncertainty estimates. The auxiliary confirmation uses two runs, while the primary long-horizon comparison has one trajectory per arm.
record.rows_left_out: No cap-driven omissions. Table 12's separate clean–corrupt and binding-swap values, its top domain-probe panel, and other training metrics are not separately recorded here because the bottom-panel functional and causal measures plus the direct induction AUC/order results were prioritized; the top panel's flattened values do not align unambiguously with all printed headers.

untested.parts: Attention-only transformers. Composition with a previous-token head is shown only as a positive binding-ablation drop in Pythia 160M, with no QK/OV composition analysis.
Abruptness, a narrow window, coincidence with an ICL gain and a loss bump: all untested.
Other families, architectures and modalities. Only Pythia 160M (two runs) and one 1.485B GPT decoder are tested.
Persistence of in-context learning (token-index loss) under different data.
Overlapping transitions in loss or ICL. Only role-selectivity trajectories are shown.

missing.what: First value column of Table 12 bottom (.042/.069/.098/.041/.048/.093, clean selectivity) and the negative swap column (−.163 to −.329), both reported as gates
Ambiguous-recall NLL direction across three independent 3B initializations: lower, lower, higher by 0.00321
Formation vs endpoint teacher ambiguous-recall NLL trajectory, mixed at early checkpoints
Binding and matching role-selectivity values over checkpoints per arm

record.verdict_notes: The text asserts that Joint-to-matching improves induction within both teachers, but Table 14 shows endpoint-teacher induction AUC .6996 < .7141. Induction measures serve mainly as diagnostics for a data-selection method, so the V5 evidence is intervention-driven, though the Ordinary arm gives natural formation. Six reader rows misparse Table 12.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests functional binding, matching, and value transport, but does not directly establish composition with an earlier previous-token head or test the exact [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism in attention-only transformers.
No test of abrupt emergence in a narrow window coinciding with an in-context-learning gain or a bump in the training loss.
No test of whether induction heads account for most token-index in-context learning in large transformers.
The tested evidence is limited to the reported model settings and does not establish universality across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
The study tests data-selection and ordering effects on its functional circuit measures, but not whether in-context learning persists under different data and training setups.
No comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.

The study measures binding, matching, and transport as distinct functional stages, but does not compare a single-transition account against every possible alternative account of induction-head formation.
